To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the QuikSACAT radar measurements of tropical cyclones have been analyzed to develop a new geophysical model function that accounts for the effects of rain and is more suitable to the extreme high wind conditions of tropical cyclones than the NSCAT2 model function.
the QuikScat radar measurements of Hurricane Floyd have been analyzed and used to develop a geophysical model function of the Ku-band radar /sigma/0/ for extreme high wind speeds.

(1) The NSCAT2 GMFs are not suitable for QuikSCAT measurements of extreme high winds in hurricanes; (2) the rain rate is a significant factor in determining the QuikSCat /spl sigma//sup 0/ values for hurricanes; (3) the modified GMF improves QuikSCAT retrievals of Hurricane Floyd in 2000; and (4) the QuikSCA wind retrievals agree well with the NOAA HRD analyses.
In summary, our research is concerned with
developing an accurate geophysical model function and applying it to QuikSCAT measurements of tropical cyclones.
the development of the QuikSCAt GMF and application to tropical cyclones.
the development and applications of the GMF for QuikSCAT measurements of tropical cyclones, and the QuikSCAD wind estimates for Hurricane Floyed.

the QuikSat GMF is an important step forward for scatterometer applications to tropical cyclones.
the QuikScat wind estimates are useful and reliable for tropical cyclones.
the QuikScat data are useful in the study of tropical cyclones and that the Quikscat data can be used to improve the accuracy of the QuikSCat wind retrievals for tropical cyclones.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the QuikSat data is useful for tropical cyclone wind retrievals.

the QuikScat GMF can provide accurate wind retrievals for extreme wind conditions.
the QuikScat GMF for tropical cyclones should be modified to account for rain effects.
